# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages
# ask-soony

Our entry for the **Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running"** at START Hack Munich 2026.

Soony, a (fictional) games publisher, launches Grand Heist 6 on **Sunday 22 Nov, 20:00**. Every copy is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg, six suppliers deliver the parts, and the last 20% is not packed yet. Soony's data lives in SAP, spreadsheets, PDFs and scans, in four languages. Soony's head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."

We build agents that read that data, decide what is at risk and act on it before it is too late.

## Status

Work in progress. The product direction is being decided; this README will describe it once it is fixed.

## Getting started

1. Clone the repo
2. Create a `.env` in the repo root with the team token from the portal's Settings:

   ```bash
   SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN=your-team-token
   ```

3. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

Run instructions follow once the stack is in place.

## Data

All customer data comes from the Soony portal at runtime (`GET /api/v1/files`, `/api/v1/archive.zip`). It is confidential: use it only for this hackathon, never share it outside the team and never commit it (`data/` is gitignored).

- [ ] Working prototype, deployed
- [ ] Pitch deck
- [ ] Demo video, max 3 minutes
- [ ] This repo with a short README (how to run, what it does)

Live demo from Sun 14:00: 3 minutes of pitch, 2 minutes of questions.

=== Lio_-_Challenge_Keep_the_Line_Running.pdf
L I O C H A L L E N G E · S TA R T H A C K M U N I C H 2 0 2 6




Keep the Line
Running.
You just closed your first customer. They are about to ship the biggest game
release of the year, the trucks leave on Sunday at 20:00, and the last 20% is
not packed yet. They bought an AI solution to save the launch. That solution is
you. It just does not exist yet.


80% packed                                                                      The last 20% are on you




01                                           02                  03
Your first customer                          The situation       Your mission

04                                           05                  06
Your toolkit                                 Office hours        Demo, prize & good to know
 01 YOUR FIRST CUSTOMER



Congrats.
You just sold an AI solution.
Lio does not run procurement for itself. We run it for the companies that hire us. This
weekend, you sit in that seat: a young startup with one paying customer, a hard deadline, and
a chance to prove you are worth the contract.

Meet Soony
A games publisher you will probably recognize. Thirteen years after the last heist game, Soony is about to
release Grand Heist 6, developed by Popstar Studios: the biggest game release of the year. Soony makes
nothing itself. Six suppliers deliver the parts, and every copy is packed in one place: Soony’s distribution
center in Hamburg. From there, trucks take it to retailers across Europe, and fans who pre-ordered the
numbered Collector’s Edition are counting the hours.


   Sun 20:00                            640,000                          72,000                              6
   Grand Heist 6 goes on                Standard copies                  numbered Collector’s                suppliers, 1 distribution
   sale. Trucks leave                   needed on day one                Editions, all pre-                  center
   Hamburg.                                                              ordered

Soony, Popstar Studios and Grand Heist 6 are entirely fictional. Any resemblance to a certain publisher, a certain studio and a certain
game you may have waited a while for is purely coincidental.


     “Our fans have waited years for this game. If it is not on the shelf on Sunday,
     nobody will remember the game. They will remember that we missed it.”
     Soony, the morning after they signed with you


What you sold them
Honestly? The sales call was a little vague. Soony panicked, they bought AI, and they expect it to work by
Sunday. These are the notes from your onboarding meeting. You find them in the data as
soony/context/onboarding_notes.md:



     Kickoff w/ Soony – notes (11 Nov)

     - launch: Sun 22 Nov, 20:00. 487k pre-orders. date cannot move.
     - SAP has the purchase orders. nothing else. rest = Excel, PDFs, paper
     - suppliers write in their own language: KR, CN, PL, EN
     - ~20 open shipments in a spreadsheet, updated "when someone remembers"
     - head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."
     - why us: suppliers flag problems too late. launch at risk, every fix expensive
     - on the data: "It is what it is."
     - first demo: Sunday (!!)




Lio Challenge · Keep the Line Running
 0 2 T H E S I T U AT I O N



80% Packed.
The last 20% are on you.
The game is finished. The boxes, cards and editions are mostly in Hamburg, and the packing
lines are running. But the last stretch is where launches die: a part that is not there, a truck
that does not come, a number in the system that is not true.

              Standard Edition                                                            512,000 of 640,000 packed at kickoff




              Collector’s Edition                                                           46,800 of 72,000 packed at kickoff



                Packed         Still open: your job

What everybody at Soony agrees on
LAUNCH                        Grand Heist 6 goes on sale Sunday, 22 November, 20:00. The trucks to retail leave
                              Hamburg from 20:00. Whatever is not on them misses launch day.

WHERE                         Everything is packed at one site: the distribution center in Hamburg. There is no plan B
                              site.

TIME                          Saturday 06:00–22:00 and Sunday 06:00–20:00. 30 hours of packing. No night shift.

SUPPLIERS                     Six suppliers deliver what goes into the box. What is ordered now will mostly arrive too
                              late.

W H Y S O L AT E ?            The game master was finished late, and the programmed game cards only started arriving
                              three weeks ago.




     “The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not.”
     Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.


Lio Challenge · Keep the Line Running
 03 YOUR MISSION



Play the Startup.
The solution is up to you.
We do not prescribe a technology, an architecture or a product idea. You decide what to
build, you build it, you pitch it. Like a real founding team.

   YO U D E C I D E                                                         YO U G E T
   The pain point you want to own                                           A customer with a real problem

   The product                                                              Their messy data, and a world that keeps moving

   The tech: software, hardware, voice, anything                            Their suppliers, who write back

   The business model                                                       Three people from their team to interview




                                     Agents do real work.
       THE ONE RULE
                                     Your AI reads, decides and acts. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.


Do not build everything. Nobody saves a launch in 30 hours by fixing everything. Pick the pain that excites
you most, one the customer’s team tells you about or one nobody has noticed yet, and go deep.

Ten directions to get you thinking
Not a checklist. Pick one, combine three, or ignore all of them.

Lio Challenge · Keep the Line Running
 04 YOUR TOOLKIT



Everything a real
customer would give you.
Soony opens its doors to you, like a real customer on day one of a project: data, suppliers,
people. Some of it is clean. Most of it is not.

   C U S T O M E R P O R TA L                                 S U P P L I E R I N B OX
   Their data and every new drop                              Write to suppliers. They write back.
   Soony gives you access to its data through a               Want something from a supplier? Email them.
   portal, in the browser and through an API.                 Where to reach them, and how they react, is yours
   Everything you need at kickoff is there, and every         to find out. Agent to agent, if you dare.
   new release lands there too.
   start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-0
   1.azurewebsites.net




What you get at kickoff
The data is realistic, which means it is messy, incomplete and occasionally contradicts itself. There are
things hidden in it that a careful team will find.
   Master data: products, editions, bills of materials,        Transactions: purchase orders, goods receipts,
   suppliers, sites.                                           stock, shipments.

   Documents: contracts and supplier documents                 Context: how Soony’s procurement is organized, its
   (order confirmations, notices, scans), in more than         policies, and your onboarding notes.
   one format.

The world keeps moving
Real supply chains do not sit still, and neither does this one. New information shows up in the portal during
the hack, unannounced, just like in real life, where you never have everything you need on day one. You do
not have to react to every drop. Use what helps your product and your story. And do not worry: it is sleep-
friendly. Not even Soony works at night.




   LOGISTICS                            SUPPLIERS             CUSTOMER                     NEWS
   Shipments and                        Messages and          New requests and             What happens in the
   trucks that do not go                documents that        rules from Soony.            world and touches
   to plan.                             change the picture.                                the launch.




Lio Challenge · Keep the Line Running
 04 YOUR TOOLKIT



Plug in your agents.
Portal, API, inbox.
Your agents will want the data and the suppliers without a human clicking around. Here is
how to connect them.

The portal
1 · Register                            Register your team, then log in with the team name and password.

2 · Data view                           Browse the current state, folder by folder. New drops show up as a notification,
                                        and the page updates by itself.

3 · Settings                            Your team token for the API, and the sender addresses for supplier email. Office
                                        hours are booked in the portal too.


The API
Authenticate with your team token from Settings. The full docs are in the portal.

    GET /api/v1/files                              Every file with size, checksum and URL
    GET /api/v1/files/{path}                       One file

    GET /api/v1/archive.zip                        Everything at once
    GET /api/v1/openapi.json                       The OpenAPI spec


Emailing suppliers
    Register your senders first. In Settings, add every address your team or your agents send from. Mail from
    other addresses gets no reply.

Tech setup
Any stack. Any language, framework, model or orchestration. Your call. Stuck on something technical? Lio
engineers are at the booth all weekend.




Lio Challenge · Keep the Line Running
 05 OFFICE HOURS

content.text:
I read the challenge brief, the judging sheet and the deep-dive slides. **The first thing to do is get the data, and that's blocked on one thing from you.** `.env` exists, but `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` is empty, and the API answers `401 unauthorized` without it. Nothing useful can be built before we've seen the files.

**What to do now, in order:**

1. **Token and sender addresses (5 min).** In the portal, register the team if nobody has yet. Under Settings, copy the team token into `.env` and add every email address the agents will send from; suppliers don't reply to unregistered senders.
2. **Book office hours.** Talks are Sat 14:00, Sat 17:00 and Sun 09:00, one talk per block, assigned by lottery. 14:00 has probably passed, so get into the 17:00 lottery. The judges explicitly reward "On Saturday, Felix told us… so we built…", so this counts toward the score.
3. **I pull the archive into `data/` and map it (about 30 min).** I'll write a small fetch script (`archive.zip`, plus a re-sync that diffs checksums so new drops show up). Then I'll do a first read across master data, POs, stock, shipments and documents. In particular I'll do the feasibility math: open quantity × bill of materials against stock plus inbound shipments, and against pack capacity (3 lines for Standard, 1 manual cell for Collector's, 30 hours). That tells us where the launch actually breaks. The brief hints the system says "fine" while the gut says otherwise.
4. **Choose the direction once we know what's broken, by around 17:00.** My guess is the Collector's Edition: it's only 65% packed, has 7 parts and goes through one manual cell.

**My recommended product shape:** a "Launch Control" agent that recomputes whether Sunday 20:00 is reachable every time a new file lands. It flags contradictions instead of resolving them silently, and then acts: it emails the supplier who owns the gap and handles the reply. It also hands Maren a recommendation with a price on it and a one-click approve. That covers the "agents act" rule, messy data, new drops and the judges' "one click to act". It's a guess until we've seen the data.

The data is confidential, so I'll keep it in `data/` (gitignored) and never put values in code.

# Kickoff with Soony – onboarding notes

Date: 2026-11-11
Attendees: Jonas Lindqvist (CPO), Dr. Maren Vogt (Head of Procurement), Raj Patel (Logistics), us

## What they said

- Grand Heist 6 goes on sale on Sunday 22 November 2026 at 20:00. The date is fixed by retail and by 487,000 pre-orders. "Produced" means packed at the distribution center in Hamburg (DC-HAM).
- Two editions. Standard: game card, case, sleeve, leaflet. Collector's: numbered, 72,000 copies, all pre-ordered, with steel case, art book, poster and a statue.
- The developer finished the game master late. Programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago, so Hamburg packs until the last hour.
- Since the first game cards arrived it has been crisis mode: buyers chasing suppliers by phone every day, freight rebooked from sea to air and back, every shift packing whatever arrived that day. Maren: "We get through by working around problems, not by solving them. The team is exhausted."
- The last 20 % will have no buffer. Jonas: "One late pallet on launch weekend and fans who paid for a numbered Collector's Edition get nothing."
- Why us: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They need help now, before the launch, not next quarter. Jonas: "We cannot afford a single surprise in the last days before the launch."
- Six suppliers, and procurement knows them through paper: contracts, order confirmations, delivery notes. Every supplier has its own folder now. "Half of what we know is in a PDF somebody scanned."
- SAP holds the purchase orders, nothing else. There are two exports because the interface changed in mid-2025.
- Maren: suppliers tell them about problems too late. "We find out at the dock."
- Raj: about 20 open shipments, tracked in a shared spreadsheet that is updated when someone remembers.
- Delivery notes are scanned by the receiving team in Hamburg. Receiving books what is on the paper.
- Suppliers write in their own language. Nobody in procurement reads Polish or Korean.
- The Category Lead for Collector's Items left in the summer. The position is open.

## Open questions we did not get to

- What does a missing copy cost on day one? (Maren: "ask me at the booth")
- Who signs off on air freight?
- Which parts have only one source?
- Why does the stock list show no lid magnets?

## Data they gave us

See the portal: one folder per supplier under `suppliers/`, Soony's own data under `soony/`. They warned us: "It is what it is."

 Procurement Policy PP-07 · Approval of purchase orders and
 supplier releases
 Version 3.2 · Effective 2025-04-01 · Owner: Head of Procurement · Review: annually



 1. Purpose
 This policy defines who may approve purchase orders (POs), supplier releases and air-freight spend.

 2. Approval limits by value (per PO, in EUR)
                         Role                                                Limit per PO
                         Buyer                                               < 50,000
                         Category Lead                                       < 500,000
                         Head of Procurement                                 < 2,000,000
                         Chief Procurement Officer                           < 5,000,000
                         CPO and CFO jointly                                 ≥ 5,000,000


 3. Receiving site
 POs delivered to a Soony site require, in addition to the value approval, a booked dock slot released by the site
 lead.
  Site                                         Site lead                                    Deputy
  DC-HAM Hamburg                               Katrin Jansen                                Raj Patel


 4. Air freight
 Unplanned air freight up to EUR 200,000 per calendar month and category is approved by the responsible
 Category Lead. Above that, approval by the CPO is required before booking.

 5. New suppliers
 A supplier is released for serial deliveries only after a successful PPAP and written release by the Supplier
 Quality Lead and the responsible Category Lead. Conditional releases are limited to 90 days from the date of
 release. POs placed after a conditional release has expired are held in status 'awaiting approval'. A conditional
 release is extended in writing, once and by at most 90 days, by the responsible Category Lead together with the
 Supplier Quality Lead.

 6. Exceptions
 Exceptions must be documented and approved by the Head of Procurement.

# Data findings, Sat 21 Nov ~14:30 (kickoff drop)

Confidential: lives in gitignored data/, never commit or share outside the team.

## Headline
The official launch plan (status Fri 18:00) marks every part "ok" and only flags lid magnets.
The magnets are a false alarm; the real risks are elsewhere and all hit the Collector's Edition (CE).

## Real risks
1. Art books (CMP-GAM-008): GR 5000413065 booked 80,000 vs 8,000 ordered ("over delivery accepted").
   Scan WZ-261116-473: 80.000 crossed out, 8 000 handwritten; weight 360 kg fits 8k, not 80k.
   Real stock ~19,300, not 91,300. Need 25,200, so ~5,900 short.
   Karton Nowak bindery down Sat 14:00 to Mon 06:00; rush clause §3.2 covers sleeves/leaflets/posters only.
   Only rescue: finished art books in Nowak's warehouse (notice says shipping finished goods is possible), express truck Poznań to DC-HAM is 1 day.
2. Statues (CMP-GAM-010): lot 5000413063 (5,600, Pune) failed AQL 1.0 (9/125 paint defects) but is booked unrestricted.
   Usable 21,800 vs 25,200 needed, so ~3,400 short. Concession needs Supplier Quality + Category Lead Collector's Items, and that post is vacant.
   Pune's conditional release (2026-08-01, 90 days per PP-07 §5) has expired; newer POs sit in awaiting_approval.
   Pune OCs claim "approved for serial supply", which contradicts the contract §2.2 and the profile ("conditional").
3. CE pack rate: the plan assumes 900/h (28 of 30 h). Best real day in the packout log is 6,800 units. Weekday shift hours unknown: ask.
4. Sleeve artwork (CMP-GAM-004): PackRight OCs print rev B; Karton Nowak prints rev C (USK 2026, from Soony Marketing 2026-08-07). Master data says rev B.
   Stock: 122k Nowak + 64k PackRight. If rev C is the valid one, 64k PackRight sleeves are unusable (Nowak §6.2: superseded artwork not accepted).
   Then 122k + 20k Nowak road (ETA Sat) = 142k vs 128k needed: tight but ok.
5. Card cases (CMP-GAM-003): 96k stock vs 128k needed. 350k container discharged at CTA Hamburg since 19 Nov (ERP), tracker still says "in transit, RP: call terminal".
   Needs truck pick-up + dock slot (PP-07 §3: Katrin Jansen / Raj Patel).
6. Game cards (CMP-GAM-001): 118,400 + 48,000 air from ICN (ETA FRA Sat, +1 day road) = 166,400 vs 153,200. Ok only if that air shipment lands; status still "booked".

## False alarms / noise
- Lid magnets: fitted by PackRight into the Collector's Box (contract Annex A/B, components.csv note). BOM double-counts them.
- 78,000 PRM-GH6-PIN (pre-order enamel pins, Dongguan) booked to misc merchandise, no PO, no BOM. Possibly meant for pre-order packs: ask.
- Boise OCs say EXW, SAP says DDP Hamburg: cost/risk issue, not a launch blocker.
- Small price variances on delivered POs.

## Seeds for later drops
- PackRight §8: rare-earth export restrictions are force majeure; magnets come from Jiangxi RareMag (Ganzhou).
- Hwaseong LTA expires 2026-12-31.
- Dongguan: Chinese New Year shutdown schedule due by 30 Nov.
- 11 goods receipts have no scan.

## Approvals (PP-07)
Buyer < 50k EUR, Category Lead < 500k, Head of Procurement < 2M, CPO < 5M. Air freight > 200k/month/category needs CPO.
Exceptions: Head of Procurement (Maren). Category Lead Collector's Items: vacant.
